findings.source_quote: μετὰ τῶν ἐπομένων μοι δακτυλίων καὶ ὑποδήσεων
findings.english_quote: together with the rings and footwear that go with them
findings.issue: The draft makes the rings and footwear accompany the linen garments. The supplied μοι instead identifies Peter as the person whom they accompany or with whom they are associated. The draft introduces a relationship to the garments that the Greek does not supply.
findings.suggested_revision: Replace this phrase with “together with the rings and footwear that accompany me.” The replacement requires fresh review.

findings.english_quote: The understood subject is Clement’s mother and brothers, since the messengers themselves necessarily went to Athens. ἐπιδημέω can mean be present, reside, or arrive as a visitor.
findings.issue: The family is a defensible contextual subject, and the main text’s “they” can preserve the referent uncertainty. However, the note presents that subject categorically and dismisses the messengers through an assertion of necessity. The surrounding infinitives have the messengers as their understood subject, so their continuing as subject here remains a grammatical alternative, particularly with the sense “had stayed/resided.” Being sent to Athens does not by itself establish that they stayed there. This is ordinary referent ambiguity, not source corruption.
findings.suggested_revision: Revise the note to say: “Here ‘they’ is taken as Clement’s mother and brothers, because the searchers were sent to Athens and their report concerns the missing family. Alternatively, the continuing subject may be the searchers, reporting that they had not stayed in Athens itself. The Greek does not explicitly mark a change of subject.” The main pronoun may remain, but the revised disclosure requires fresh review.

findings.source_quote: τῶν οὖν πολλὰ λεγόντων ἑωρακέναι πτώματα κατὰ πολλοὺς τόπους
findings.english_quote: When many said that they had seen corpses in many places
findings.issue: πολλὰ is neuter accusative plural, not a masculine genitive quantifying the speakers. It naturally modifies πτώματα across the intervening words: “many corpses.” An adverbial attachment to λεγόντων, expressing much speaking, is also possible. The draft instead assigns its quantity to the people and represents neither attachment faithfully.
findings.suggested_revision: Use “When those people said that they had seen many corpses in many places,” and add a note explaining that πολλὰ is taken with πτώματα, supported by their agreement and the parallel reference to many places. Preserve the alternative attachment to λεγόντων as “those who spoke at length, saying that they had seen corpses in many places.” The replacement and note require fresh review.

findings.source_quote: ἤδη λοιπὸν ἔκτοτε εἰκοστὸν ἔτος ἐστίν, ἀφ’ ἧς οὐδεμίαν τινὰ περὶ αὐτοῦ ἀλήθειαν ἤκουσα
findings.english_quote: this is now the twentieth year since then, during which I have heard no reliable news at all about him
findings.issue: “During which” can attach to the twentieth year alone. The source’s ἀφ’ ἧς expresses “since” the earlier point in time, so the absence of reliable information extends from that time to the present, not merely through the current year.
findings.suggested_revision: Clarify the temporal scope: “it is now the twentieth year since then, and I have heard no reliable news at all about him since that time.” Retain the ordinal year count. This replacement requires fresh review.
